description.en-US: The quotation this line belongs to. Immutable, for the reason the order line's is: moving a line between quotations would change two totals at once, and the one it left would keep a total it can no longer justify.

Position within the quotation, unique per quotation and starting at 1 because it appears on customer-facing paperwork. Carried onto the order line of the same number at conversion, so a customer comparing the quote to the order sees the same line in the same place.
What is being quoted. The variant, not the template, matching the order line: the variant is the transactable unit. Nullable for the same reason - a combo parent quotes no single variant.

The product code as it stood when the quotation was priced. A SNAPSHOT, like the order line's: a quotation is a statement about what was offered, and a product renamed afterwards must not silently restate it.
The product name as quoted. Snapshot for the same reason as the code.
The unit the quantity is in. A plain ulid, since units of measure belong to essential.

How much was quoted. Named plainly rather than ordered_quantity, because nothing has been ordered - and the three companion quantities an order line carries (fulfilled, returned, requires_fulfillment) are deliberately absent here for the same reason: a quotation moves no goods.

The price per unit as quoted. One column where the order line has two - base and effective - because a quotation states the offer rather than explaining how it was reached; the adjustment chain that justifies an order's number is rebuilt at conversion, when the engine runs again.
What was taken off this line.
The line total after discount and before tax.

The indicative tax on this line. Indicative because a quotation is not a fiscal document: the tax actually charged is determined when the resulting order confirms, and may differ if rates moved in between.
What this line was quoted at, all in.
